name: Calendar View
tagline: A Dataverse view as a month, week or timeline calendar, by a date column — drag to reschedule, drag a bar's edge to resize, click a day to create.

limitations: The calendar opens on September 2026, not on today. The fixture’s events are fixed dates and the harness cannot follow the clock, so the presets set the Opens on property; on a form that property is empty and the calendar opens on the user’s today.

Times are shown in your browser’s time zone. On a form the control asks userSettings.getTimeZoneOffsetMinutes() for the Dataverse user’s zone and places each event by that, which is the day the user means; the harness publishes no user settings, so the browser’s zone stands in.

Events are placed by the shape of their value rather than by the column’s behaviour. On a model-driven form the control reads each date column’s Behavior through getEntityMetadata — a User Local instant is placed in the user’s zone, a Date Only day on its day everywhere — and the harness has no metadata to read, so a value at UTC midnight is taken as a whole day and anything else as an instant.

Events carry no colour. The Kind column is bound as the colour role, and on a form each event takes its option’s colour from the option set’s metadata; the harness has no option set, so the label shows as a badge in the week view and the edge stays brand blue.

Stepping to another month does not fetch it. On a form the control sends the visible range to the server as a filter — start ≤ last day AND (end ≥ first day OR end is empty) — and refreshes; the harness discards filters, so every fixture record is loaded at once and the other months are simply empty.

Dragging an event changes nothing in Dataverse. The control writes through the record where the platform allows it and through webAPI.updateRecord() otherwise, and the harness mocks both — the event still moves, because the control places it optimistically and only retires that override once refreshed data agrees. The movedRecordId and selectedDate outputs update either way.

Resizing a bar on the timeline changes nothing in Dataverse either. Dragging an edge writes only the column that moved — the end, or the start — by the same two routes, and the bar keeps its new length here for the same reason a moved event keeps its day.

There is no + on the days. Creating opens the table’s quick create form through navigation.openForm with the day passed as a form parameter, and the harness has no forms to open, so the button is hidden here the way it is in a canvas app.
Load more never appears. The harness puts every fixture record on a single page and reports hasNextPage as false; on a form a month with more events than the page size offers the rest.
Clicking an event calls dataset.openDatasetItem(), which the harness logs as a mock call. The openedRecordId output still updates.

presets.name: Month
presets.description: September 2026 as a month grid: a three-day offsite, an evening dinner, a whole-day release, and a title long enough to truncate.

presets.name: Timeline
presets.description: September as one row per event with a bar from start to end. Drag a bar to move it, or its right edge to make it longer; the month scrolls sideways.

presets.name: Week
presets.description: The week of 14 September, where each event shows its time and its kind.

presets.name: Read-only, no times
presets.description: The shape for a dashboard: nothing moves, nothing opens, and a Date and Time column reads as days.
